content: <thought>The most intense peak is at m/z ≈ 199, with a comparable peak at m/z ≈ 201, indicating a bromine atom (79Br/81Br isotopic pattern). Assuming the peak is the protonated ion [M+H]⁺, the neutral mass is ≈ 197.99 Da. Subtracting the monoisotopic mass of 79Br (78.918 Da) leaves ≈ 119.07 Da, which fits best with a C₉H₁₁ fragment (exact mass ≈ 198.004 Da for C₉H₁₁Br). This matches the observed mass within experimental error. Hence the molecular formula is C₉H₁₁Br.
